items.title: 61521_David Albert Francis oral history interview
items.q: Well, he was looking for a drummer, and I joined him.

ctx.x: Yeah. Well, he was looking for a drummer, and I joined him. And I was playing a whole lot of different hotels then, and at that time, they were still using black groups in different rooms of the different hotels, the St. Regis and all those hotels around New York. So I was playing with him, like we'd probably play 2 nights at the St. Regis, we played one night at the Astor, you know, and two nights at the Waldorf. But that's how we worked.

So, now, this is around about -- November, it's around November, so about the first of the year, I'm getting the chance to go in to the Apollo Theatre with Billy Hicks. But we got to play show. Now I can't read no music, see. I still can't read, you know.

items.title: Panama Francis interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 1, 1995
items.q: Later gigs with Billy Hicks, Roy Eldridge, Lucky Millinder and Cab Calloway made him a familiar and sought-after drummer

ctx.x: Drummer David “Panama” Francis has been performing professionally since the 1930’s. A native of Miami, David played his first engagements with the Florida Collegians and in New York with Tab Smith. Later gigs with Billy Hicks, Roy Eldridge, Lucky Millinder and Cab Calloway made him a familiar and sought-after drummer for both recordings and live shows. The studios in New York City have called on Panama frequently since the 1950’s and he has played on hundreds of Jazz, Rhythm & Blues and early Rock records. In…
